name: Queensland
note: Queensland's Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2023 (in force 24 June 2024) puts the duty to apply for registration on a spouse or relative within 14 days of death, though a funeral director usually lodges it; the doctor's cause of death certificate is due within 2 working days and reportable deaths go to police or a coroner. The Queensland registrar coordinates national death data for all Australian registries and, under s 118, may make arrangements with government agencies and private organisations, including to remove deceased persons from their databases (the Australian Death Check).

steps.title: Reportable death reported to police or a coroner
steps.who: A person who becomes aware of a death that may be reportable.
steps.trigger: A violent, unnatural, suspicious, health-care-related, in-care or in-custody death, an unidentified body, or no cause of death certificate issued.
steps.summary: The report goes to a police officer or coroner; police pass it to a coroner in writing.

steps.title: Coroner releases the body for burial
steps.trigger: Autopsy finished or body no longer needed.
steps.summary: In a coronial case the coroner's release order, not a doctor's certificate, allows disposal; a doctor must not issue a cause of death certificate for an apparently reportable death unless a coroner advises.

steps.title: Doctor issues the cause of death certificate
steps.who: A doctor who attended the person, examined the body or considered the medical history and can form an opinion on the probable cause.

deadline.text: within 2 working days of the death or finding of the body

steps.summary: The doctor gives the original certificate, in an approved way, to the person arranging disposal (or to the registrar) and a copy to that person. A doctor who may benefit from the death must not certify.

steps.title: Spouse or relative applies to register the death
steps.who: A spouse or relative of the deceased; the registrar may instead require the person in charge of the place of death, the finder of the body, or the person arranging disposal (e.g. a funeral director).

deadline.text: within 14 days after the death or the finding of the body

steps.summary: The application is made in the registrar's form and approved way, with the required certificates; failure is an offence (20 penalty units). In practice a funeral director lodges it. Late applications can be accepted.

steps.title: Person arranging disposal passes the cause of death certificate to the registrar
steps.who: The person arranging disposal of the body.
steps.summary: The original cause of death certificate reaches the registrar through the person arranging disposal.

steps.title: Notice of disposal of the body to the registrar
steps.who: The person who disposes of the body (e.g. a funeral director).
steps.summary: A separate notice of disposal is due within 7 days of burial or cremation (20 penalty units), with further notices for removal from Queensland or failure to dispose within 30 days.

steps.title: Registrar registers the death
steps.who: The Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages (Queensland).
steps.summary: The registrar enters the death in the register of deaths and may do so while a coroner is still investigating.

steps.title: Death certificate issued to applicants with an adequate reason
steps.who: Any entity may apply; the registrar may refuse an applicant without an adequate reason, weighing relationship to the deceased and intended use.
steps.summary: Certificates are restricted by an adequate-reason test rather than a closed list of relatives.

steps.title: Registrar shares death information with government agencies under arrangements
steps.who: The registrar, under an arrangement with a government agency (policy, service delivery, research) found to be in the public interest.
steps.summary: Section 118 is the general Queensland power behind data feeds to government, including the national fact-of-death data Queensland coordinates for all registries.

steps.title: Registrar notifies child-death registrations
steps.who: The registrar, to the family and child commissioner and the chief executive (child safety).

deadline.text: within 30 days after registering the death

steps.summary: Child deaths are notified to the child-death review bodies.

steps.title: Registrar sends monthly death lists to the AEC
steps.who: The Queensland registrar as Registrar-General under the Commonwealth Electoral Act.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death of a person aged 16 or over.

deadline.text: after the beginning of each month

steps.summary: Commonwealth law; see the au-commonwealth layer.

steps.title: Arrangements to cleanse organisations' databases of deceased persons (Australian Death Check)
steps.who: Non-government organisations, private sector agencies and government agencies under an arrangement with the registrar; Queensland runs the national Australian Death Check for all registries.
steps.trigger: Standing arrangement; the organisation submits its records.
steps.summary: The Act expressly authorises arrangements to remove the names of deceased persons from organisations' databases, the statutory footing for the Australian Death Check administered by the Queensland Registry.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Application to register within 14 days after the death or finding of the body; late applications may be accepted.

informantDuty.note: A spouse or relative must apply; the registrar may require the person in charge of the place, the finder or the person arranging disposal instead.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review; the certifying doctor is barred only for reportable deaths or personal benefit.

electronicRegistration.note: The Act requires the application 'in an approved way' without specifying electronic lodgement; the Queensland Government BDM site was unreachable.

certificateAccess.note: Any entity may apply but the registrar may refuse without an adequate reason (relationship, use).

gaps: Who may verify (pronounce) death: no Queensland statute found.

Rechecked 28 October 2026: the 15 quotes from the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2023 were compared against the authorised PDF (www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/pdf/inforce/current/act-2023-017, current as at 16 September 2026). All 15 are verbatim, apart from spacing the PDF text layer splits inside words, and each sits in the section its citation names.

The four Coroners Act 2003 quotes (ss 7, 8, 26(3), 26(5)) are still unchecked character for character: the same host answers the Coroners Act PDF with an Incapsula challenge, which was not bypassed.
